newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity called lower amid nuke restarts.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity called lower amid nuke restarts.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures were called to open lower Monday on weekend restarts of two West nuclear power plants and light air-conditioning demand in the Northwest, market sources said.
Referring to the nuclear plant restarts, an East Coast power broker said, "That and the non-eventful weather are pushing prices lower."

In over-the-counter trading, August Palo Verde PV) futures were discussed at $33.75-34.25 a megawatt hour (MWh) versus Thursday's settlement at $34.35 and August California-Oregon Border (COB) was quoted near $22.75-23.00 against Thursday's close at $23.02.
NYMEX was closed Friday in observance of U.S. Independence Day.

PG&E Corp's 1,073 megawatt (MW) Diablo Canyon 2 nuclear power unit on the central California coast reached 50 percent power early Monday after being manually shut July 2 because of problems with its feedwater system.
The 1,158 MW WNP-2 nuclear power plant in Washington state was in a startup mode as of early today but had not yet reconnected to the electricity grid.
Moreover, the 1,221 MW Palo Verde 3 nuclear unit near Phoenix, Ariz., returned to 100 percent output over the weekend after a 15 percent load reduction for repairs late last week.

Almost 2,500 MW of coal-fired generation in the West were scheduled to resume production by today. They included two 670 MW Centralia units in Washington, 330 MW Colstrip units in Montana, a 260 MW Hayden unit in Colorado and a 550 MW Laramie River unit in Wyoming.
Meteorlogists called for wet and cool weather staying over the Pacific Northwest this week before a warming trend begins early next week.
Meanwhile, temperatures are projected to average near normal over most of the Southwest but below normal in the far northeast region and above normal the extreme southwest area.
On the downside, August PV will likely test chart support at $33.00 and August COB at $22.00, brokers and analysts said.
The 1,070 MW San Onofre 2 was shut June 29 to replace its charge line check valves, and the 1,080 MW San Onofre 3 has been offline since April 12 for refueling and maintenance.
San Onofre units 2 and 3 were expected to resume operation around July 15 and July 10, respectively.
